\section*{Question 1}

Let \(R\) be the region in the first and second quadrants bounded above by the graph of \(y=\frac{20}{1+x^{2}}\) and below by the horizontal line \(y=2\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Find the area of \(R\).
\item[(b)] Find the volume of the solid generated when \(R\) is rotated about the \(x\)-axis.
\item[(c)] The region \(R\) is the base of a solid. For this solid, the cross sections perpendicular to the \(x\)-axis are semicircles. Find the volume of this solid.
\end{itemize}
\[
\frac{20}{1+x^{2}}=2 \text { when } x= \pm 3
\]
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Area \(=\int_{-3}^{3}\left(\frac{20}{1+x^{2}}-2\right) d x=37.961\) or 37.962
\item[(b)] Volume \(=\pi \int_{-3}^{3}\left(\left(\frac{20}{1+x^{2}}\right)^{2}-2^{2}\right) d x=1871.190\)
\item[(c)] Volume \(=\frac{\pi}{2} \int_{-3}^{3}\left(\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{20}{1+x^{2}}-2\right)\right)^{2} d x\)
\[
=\frac{\pi}{8} \int_{-3}^{3}\left(\frac{20}{1+x^{2}}-2\right)^{2} d x=174.268
\]
\end{itemize}

1 : correct limits in an integral in
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] , (b), or (c)
\item[] \(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { integrand } \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}2: \text { integrand } \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}2: \text { integrand } \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\end{itemize}
